notes: Fifty-eight environmental review projects whose Internet Archive titles carry a street address somewhere other than the first position - the group the leading-digit filter that defined the address-titled set never reached. One document per project: the draft EIR where a project has one, otherwise the mitigated negative declaration, the initial study, or, where the collection holds nothing fuller, the notice of preparation. The richest are 1634-1690 Pine Street (five Auto Row buildings of 1912-1917, three of them by Heiman and Schwartz), the 50 First Street project (four named and dated buildings of the First and Mission Historic District), CityPlace at 935-965 Market Street (the Pantages, a Paff & Baur front and John Galen Howard's Empress Theater), One Rincon Hill (Lewis P. Hobart's Union Oil Company Building of 1940-41 and its clock tower), 1000 Broadway (the first house on Russian Hill and the architects who followed it) and 46 Geary Street (two 1906-07 buildings by Meyer and O'Brien and by Bliss and Faville, welded into one behind a 1956 curtain wall).

findings.description: The First Methodist Church, later St. John's United, was built here in 1911 to the design of George Washington Kramer (1847-1938) — the only building in San Francisco known to be his. It was rated "1" in the 1976 citywide architectural survey, and was vacant and proposed for demolition by 2006.
